title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed (ditto, blue ink) page of a Bourbaki draft: rédaction n° 392, page 4-42. It belongs to the draft of Algèbre commutative, ch. VII 'Diviseurs', §4 (modules over Krull domains), and is interleaved in cote 60 among Grothendieck's handwritten notes on the trace formula and functional equation of L-functions. The neighbouring pages are handwritten and concern inertia invariants and decomposition groups, so they do not continue this text. Presumably the typescript was reused as scrap paper, or simply filed there.

Mathematics on the page.

(1) End of the proof of the structure theorem (AC VII §4 n°9, Th. 6). Let A be a Krull domain (in the published version, an integrally closed noetherian domain suffices) and M a finitely generated torsion-free A-module of rank n. Then M has a free submodule L with M/L isomorphic to an ideal of A.
- The proof is by induction on n; the case n = 1 is trivial.
- For n ≥ 2, Lemma 8 gives a free rank-1 submodule L_0 with M/L_0 torsion-free, hence of rank n−1.
- Induction gives a free L_1 ⊂ M/L_0 with (M/L_0)/L_1 isomorphic to an ideal.
- Let L be the inverse image of L_1 in M. Then 0 → L_0 → L → L_1 → 0 splits because L_1 is free, so L ≅ L_0 ⊕ L_1 is free, and M/L ≅ (M/L_0)/L_1.
- A remark (with an exercise number left blank) says that M reflexive does not imply M/L reflexive.

(2) n°10, modules over Dedekind domains.
- Primes of height 1 are maximal and are the only nonzero primes. The divisor group D(A) is identified with the group I(A) of nonzero fractional ideals.
- Prop. 21: over a Dedekind domain every pseudo-null module is zero. Hence pseudo-injective, pseudo-surjective, pseudo-bijective and pseudo-null homomorphisms are respectively injective, surjective, bijective and zero.
- Prop. 22: for M finitely generated, torsion-free ⇔ reflexive ⇔ projective. The page records b ⇒ a (any domain) and c ⇒ b (Alg. II §2 n°7); the proof of a ⇒ c continues on a page not included.

These results serve the classification of finitely generated modules over Krull domains up to pseudo-isomorphism. They are relevant to Iwasawa theory, but the page itself serves no purpose in the L-function notes.
errors: No mathematical errors. The splitting argument is correct.
The exercise reference in the Remark is left blank ('exerc.   '), as is typical of a draft.

ideas.what: A finitely generated torsion-free module over a Krull/normal noetherian domain contains a free submodule with quotient isomorphic to an ideal (proof by induction via a rank-1 free submodule with torsion-free quotient).
ideas.modern_name: Structure theorem for torsion-free modules over Krull domains (Bourbaki AC VII §4 Th. 6)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative ch. VII (1965), §4 n°9

ideas.what: Over a Dedekind domain, pseudo-null modules are zero, so pseudo-injective/surjective/bijective/null homomorphisms are genuinely injective/surjective/bijective/zero.
For finitely generated modules over a Dedekind domain: torsion-free ⇔ reflexive ⇔ projective.
ideas.modern_name: Finitely generated torsion-free modules over Dedekind domains are projective

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard Bourbaki draft page whose content was published essentially verbatim in Algèbre commutative ch. VII (1965). It is not Grothendieck's own mathematics and is unrelated to the surrounding L-function notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed (a Bourbaki ditto copy), not handwritten. '4 - 42 -' and 'n° 392' are the Bourbaki draft pagination and rédaction number. The '45' at bottom left is the archive's handwritten folio number.
The transcription is otherwise accurate. 'L_o' denotes L_0 (subscript zero).
